A.explanation: This loop is closed but the vertical arrow points up and the horizontal arrow points left, opposite to the weight acting down and the rod pushing right on point P.

B.explanation: The vertical down and horizontal right arrows have correct senses, but the hypotenuse points down to the right so the three arrows do not follow head-to-tail and do not close.

C.explanation: The hypotenuse points up to the left along the cable, but the vertical arrow points up and the arrows do not make a continuous head-to-tail loop.

D.explanation: The vertical down arrow is the weight, the horizontal right arrow is the rod pushing point P, and the up-left hypotenuse is the cable tension, forming a closed head-to-tail triangle.

hints: List the three forces on point P and their directions: weight of the lamp straight down, cable tension pulling up and left along the cable, and the rod force.
The horizontal pull of the cable to the left must be balanced, so the metal rod in compression must push point P horizontally to the right.
In equilibrium the three force vectors placed head-to-tail must close, so look for down plus right plus up-left making a continuous loop.
walkthrough: Identify forces at P: $W$ due to the lamp acts vertically down, tension $T$ in the cable acts from P toward the wall, up and to the left, and force $F$ from the rod acts on P.
Resolve horizontally: $T$ has a leftward component, so for zero net force the rod must push P to the right. The rod is in compression and $F$ is horizontal to the right.
For equilibrium of coplanar forces, the vector sum is zero, so the three vectors drawn head-to-tail must form a closed triangle.
Therefore the triangle must contain one side straight down for $W$, one side to the right for $F$, and one hypotenuse directed up-left parallel to the cable for $T$.
Only the triangle with vertical down, bottom side to the right, and hypotenuse up-left satisfies both direction and head-to-tail closure. This is option D.
